title: Announcing SimReady Central: An Open Library of Simulation-Ready 3D Assets for Robotics and AI Factories
gist: NVIDIA announces SimReady Central Library, a free, ungated collection of more than 2,000 simulation-ready OpenUSD assets on Hugging Face for robotics simulation and AI factory digital twins, with OEM partners including Vertiv, FANUC, Universal Robots and LG Electronics. Natural-language asset search runs on NVIDIA USD Search, and the post shows agent-assisted scene building using OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra.

insights.claim: SimReady Central Library brings together more than 2,000 simulation-ready OpenUSD assets on Hugging Face as a free, ungated starting point for physical AI training environments and AI factory digital twins.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Puts NVIDIA's OpenUSD asset standard on the main open-model distribution platform, strengthening its simulation ecosystem lock-in.
insights.quote: SimReady Central Library brings together more than 2,000 simulation-ready (SimReady) OpenUSD assets on Hugging Face

insights.claim: The library spans robot arms and grippers, warehouse equipment, racks and cooling infrastructure, and developers can check each asset's supported capabilities and combine assets from different suppliers into one scene.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Cross-supplier composability is what makes the library useful for building digital twins.

insights.claim: SimReady assets are OpenUSD models prepared with collision geometry, mass, friction, and for AI factories electrical or thermal metadata, so developers avoid manually adding simulation properties to CAD models.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: The manual conversion from CAD to simulation-ready is the bottleneck the standard targets.
insights.quote: Simulation requires additional information about how that object should be interpreted and used.

insights.claim: SimReady Foundation provides specifications, profiles and validation tools, where a profile defines the grouping of features an asset needs for a given use case, such as collision geometry, joint limits, semantic labels, and materials and sensor attributes.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Profiles let assets be validated against workflow requirements and matched to tasks.
insights.quote: A profile defines the logical grouping of features and capabilities an asset needs for a particular use case.

insights.claim: Equipment manufacturers can prepare and validate assets against SimReady requirements and publish them to the library to reach developers, letting end customers test and simulate scenarios faster while the OEMs manage their own Hugging Face datasets.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Hugging Face becomes a distribution channel for hardware vendors' digital models, a go-to-market tactic for industrial OEMs.
insights.quote: reach developers and allow their end customers to test and simulate scenarios faster

insights.claim: Vertiv is named as an AI factory OEM that can distribute server racks, cooling equipment and supporting infrastructure assets for AI factory digital twins.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Data-center infrastructure suppliers are tying their products into NVIDIA's AI factory design workflows.
insights.quote: For AI factory OEMs like Vertiv
insights.locator: Why publish OEM assets to SimReady Central?

insights.claim: Robotics OEMs named as library contributors are Comau, FANUC, Franka Robotics, Robotiq, Standard Bots and Universal Robots, offering robot arms and grippers for training and evaluation environments.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: A broad slate of industrial robot vendors is aligning with NVIDIA's simulation stack.
insights.quote: For robotics OEMs like Comau, FANUC, Franka Robotics, Robotiq, Standard Bots, and Universal Robots
insights.locator: Why publish OEM assets to SimReady Central?

insights.claim: LG Electronics, which builds home robots alongside appliances, can share assets such as refrigerators and dishwashers for household simulation, robot training, evaluation and synthetic data generation.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Household robot developers get appliance models needed for domestic simulation.
insights.quote: For OEMs like LG Electronics (LGE) that develop robots for the home alongside the appliances they work with
insights.locator: Why publish OEM assets to SimReady Central?

insights.claim: Palatial contributes the NVIDIA Robotics 1K Dataset plus complex articulated assets generated from text, images, scans, datasheets and CAD, and ForgeCAD offers articulated robotics props with high-quality textures.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Asset-generation startups use the library as a distribution channel for synthetic content.
insights.quote: For simulation asset providers like Palatial
insights.locator: Why publish OEM assets to SimReady Central?

insights.claim: OEMs contribute through a SimReady Central submission skill that validates assets against the relevant SimReady profiles, packages them and submits them for inclusion.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Agent-style tooling is used to scale asset onboarding.
insights.quote: To contribute, OEMs can use the SimReady Central submission skill
insights.locator: Why publish OEM assets to SimReady Central?

insights.claim: NVIDIA USD Search powers natural-language search in SimReady Central Library, and Hugging Face has integrated USD Search into its platform search with indexed USD properties and simulation metadata so agents can discover suitable assets.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Search integration at platform level makes NVIDIA's asset format a first-class object on Hugging Face.
insights.quote: NVIDIA USD Search powers natural-language search in SimReady Central Library
insights.locator: Build simulation environments with SimReady assets

insights.claim: Developers can use frontier models such as OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra with asset search and scene-authoring tools to find assets, write code to assemble a scene and create scenario variations, and OEMs can use Astra to refine assets against SimReady requirements.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Frontier-model agents are being positioned as the front end for industrial simulation authoring, linking OpenAI models to NVIDIA tooling.
insights.quote: Developers can use frontier models like OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra
insights.locator: Build simulation environments with SimReady assets

insights.claim: In the pick-and-place example, Astra is expected to query the SimReady Search API, reference assets into an OpenUSD stage, generate Python to assemble the workcell using a FANUC arm and Robotiq gripper in Isaac Sim with PhysX, configure the task and render a preview.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Illustrates the target agentic workflow for robot workcell design.
insights.quote: Query the SimReady Search API to find relevant assets distributed on Hugging Face

insights.claim: For AI factory layouts, Astra would assemble racks and cooling equipment into two OpenUSD layouts and generate scripts to check equipment overlaps and aisle clearances against supplied requirements.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Automated layout comparison and clearance checks could shorten AI data-center design cycles.
insights.quote: Check for equipment overlaps and clearance violations, and report any issues.

insights.claim: Developers can keep layout and task changes in separate OpenUSD layers, configure robot training and evaluation in Isaac Lab, and for AI factories connect scenes to equipment data for power distribution or cooling analysis and to live BMS and IT telemetry to keep the digital twin synchronized with the facility.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: The digital twin is pitched as a bridge from design into live AI factory operations.

insights.claim: The SimReady Central roadmap includes more OEM partners and a growing asset library, with community feedback on needed assets, runtimes and integration gaps guiding priorities.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Library breadth, not yet quantified, will determine adoption.
insights.quote: SimReady Central’s roadmap includes more OEM partners and a growing asset library
insights.locator: Help shape the next wave of assets

insights.claim: SimReady assets can populate training environments for Microduck, the open-source robot from Hugging Face and Pollen Robotics.
insights.speaker: John Kosnik
insights.so_what: Links the asset library to the open-source robot learning ecosystem.
insights.quote: These environments can support projects such as Microduck
insights.locator: Build simulation environments with SimReady assets
